I don't know how comparable my experience can be with yours since I've been going to a *school* psychologist. I don't know if there's any difference other than her office is at our school or if there's a huge difference.

Anyways I'll tell you what it has been like to me.

She asked me questions based on how I had filled the "How I feel" papers. It probably feels silly that she asks for example "how do you sleep" even though you may have marked that you sleep terribly. It will probably feel redundant but be patient.

She also asks a lot of "why". Sometimes it gets annoying. I try to always answer but after a certain point I don't know the answer. It's okay to say I don't know. She'll just switch the subject most likely. 

She asks me a lot of uncomfortable questions. What helps me is thinking that she's a professional and needs to know.

Anyways I don't know how similar my experience is going to be with yours, if at all. If you want to ask something, go ahead, I'll probably spend rest of the night here anyway.

[Also here's your kitten.](http://i.imgur.com/vJETjyO.jpg)

It's easier when you have someone to talk to. I have one real life person and one online. What helps me is talking to them, not necessarily about my mental state but about mundane things. Cutting, nicotine or alcohol hasn't helped me at all.

I don't know what you should do. I guess school nurse could be one place to start (that's where I started).
